extracted.intended_audience: general public and stakeholders interested in FDA regulatory process (citizens, advocacy groups, pharmaceutical companies, lawyers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive standards for making and understanding FDA citizen petitions under U.S. law (how they are defined, who may file, what may be requested, statutory limits and timelines, and common uses/abuses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / purpose of FDA citizen petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An FDA citizen petition is a process provided by the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for individuals and community organizations to make requests to the FDA for changes to health policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic description of the mechanism: a pathway for interested persons to ask the FDA to act on regulations, orders, or other administrative matters affecting public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory citation (21 CFR Part 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The citizen petition process is described in Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations (21 CFR Part 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be submitted and considered under the procedures and definitions contained in 21 CFR Part 10; applicants and reviewers should consult that regulation for procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible filer — 'interested person'
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time, any 'interested person' can request that the FDA 'issue, amend, or revoke a regulation or order,' or 'take or refrain from taking any other form of administrative action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'interested person' is broad: individuals, community organizations, and companies can file petitions. Eligibility is not limited to regulated firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A citizen petition may request that the FDA 'issue, amend, or revoke a regulation or order,' or 'take or refrain from taking any other form of administrative action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should focus on concrete administrative or regulatory actions (new or changed regulations/orders or other FDA administrative actions); requests outside that scope may be less likely to be acted on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on delaying ANDA approvals and statutory response deadline (Section 505(q))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 505(q) provides that the FDA could not delay approving an ANDA due to concerns raised in a citizen petition unless the delay was 'necessary to protect public health issues'; it also mandated that the FDA needed to respond to a petition within 180 days—this was shortened to 150 days via a 2011 amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When petitions target Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs), FDA responses are time-limited and petitions cannot be used to indefinitely delay generic approvals; the statutory language conditions delay on demonstrable public-health necessity and imposes a firm response timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common use by innovators to challenge ANDAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovator companies may present arguments to the FDA that the Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) should not be accepted by filing a 'citizen petition' with the FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, many citizen petitions are filed by brand-name drug companies against competitors. Recognize this common strategic use when evaluating motives and substance of petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse and policy concerns (delaying generics / antitrust implications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharmaceutical companies routinely use FDA citizen petitions to delay the entry of generic drugs into the United States marketplace; there are concerns and analyses about abuse of the process and calls for antitrust challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because petitions can be used strategically to impede competition, reviewers and policymakers consider both legal and policy implications; evidence of abusive or dilatory filings may affect how petitions are received and could implicate antitrust review or reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA guidance to industry on submitting petitions (2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2014, the FDA issued guidance to industry about submitting citizen petitions and how it would consider them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should follow the FDA's 2014 guidance for content and format expectations and to understand how the agency evaluates petitions; the guidance provides more detailed procedural and substantive considerations than the Wikipedia summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical absence of deadlines and subsequent reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally, there was no deadline by which the FDA had to respond to citizen petitions filed to protest ANDAs, leading to significant delays in approving generics. In 2007 the law was amended (Section 505(q)) and later rules/guidance (including post-2011 amendments and FDA's 2016 update) addressed timing and other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness of the historical evolution (no deadlines → statutory amendment → FDA guidance and rulemaking) is important for understanding why current timing and limitation rules exist and how policy concerns have shaped present practice.
